research_date: Cutoff and access date: 2026-10-26. No post-cutoff release claims included. Repository creation dates are metadata, not proven public release dates.
scope: Continuation and audit of open-model-research-2026-10.md. Covers exact model identities, downloadable weights versus hosted features, reasoning/coding/tool evidence, licenses, smaller alternatives and proposed acceptance tests. Detailed hardware capacity planning belongs to item 06; no models were downloaded or run.

verified_findings.claim: The canonical released Xiaomi checkpoint is XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL: the card documents 1.02T total/42B active parameters and 1M context. Artificial Analysis links its shorter MiMo-V2.6-Pro display name to this repository. [uncertain] Separate API and downloadable checkpoint equivalence is not established.
verified_findings.confidence: High for repository identity; limited for API parity
verified_findings.practical_implication: Pin the RL repository and revision rather than selecting by display name.

verified_findings.claim: GLM-5.3 is downloadable and text-only. Its card attributes gains over GLM-5.2 to post-training. Its serving recipe documents native FP8 and a BF16 sibling. [uncertain] Recipe counts of approximately 743B/39B conflict with the 753B/40B aggregator description; exact counting conventions remain unresolved.
verified_findings.confidence: High for availability; medium for parameter accounting
verified_findings.practical_implication: Treat the exact artifact and precision as part of the candidate, and resolve counts before capacity estimates.

verified_findings.claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a downloadable multimodal update, not an API-only label. The predecessor architecture documents a 552B backbone, 196B Engram component, and 8B prefill/16B decode activation. [uncertain] The 1017 page's 763B tensor count is not reconciled to those component counts.
verified_findings.confidence: High for identity and predecessor accounting; medium for transfer to 1017
verified_findings.practical_implication: Neither 16B active nor 552B backbone is a sufficient storage requirement.

verified_findings.claim: Step 5 Preview has official weights under stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview; it documents 600B total/27B active and up to 1M context. Its license is StepFun Model License 1.0, not plain Apache 2.0.
verified_findings.practical_implication: Use the official repository rather than unrelated BF16 republishers found in search.

verified_findings.claim: Kimi K3's official repository remains accessible and describes 2.8T total/104B active, native multimodal input and 1048576 context. [uncertain] No official deprecation notice was found in the checked card; this does not establish hosted API lifecycle status.
verified_findings.confidence: High for released weights; limited for deprecation claim
verified_findings.practical_implication: Do not reject downloadable K3 because an aggregator says deprecated.

verified_findings.claim: Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is the exact downloadable artifact, with 2.4T total/95B active, text input, and 262144 native context extensible to 1010000. The card explicitly distinguishes hosted Qwen3.8-Max, which adds vision, non-thinking support, built-in tools and default 1M context.
verified_findings.practical_implication: Do not transfer API vision or context defaults to the local weights.

verified_findings.claim: Artificial Analysis displays MiMo 46, DeepSeek Flash 1017 45 and GLM-5.3 45. Its v4.3.2 methodology has ten evaluations and is primarily text-based and English-language. These are independent evaluator results for specific served configurations, not a measurement of a family's local quantization.
verified_findings.confidence: High for displayed scores; limited for local transfer
verified_findings.practical_implication: Use the index as a shortlist with version and configuration recorded.

verified_findings.claim: BenchLM's open-weight page displays MiMo 73.6 and Estimated under BenchAlign v5.8. Its methodology permits inferred composite positions from incomplete evidence and explicitly says conditional ranges do not establish rank confidence.
verified_findings.practical_implication: A leading point estimate is not verified superiority.

verified_findings.claim: Vendor coding tables do not use one common harness: GLM reports DeepSWE with mini-swe-agent and 400K context; DeepSeek 1017 uses Mini-SWE-V2 for DeepSWE and Claude Code for Terminal-Bench 4.0; Kimi mixes its own Kimi Code results with best published competitor harnesses.
verified_findings.practical_implication: Do not rank these vendor table columns as a controlled head-to-head experiment.

verified_findings.claim: Function-calling integration evidence exists: MiMo's commands select mimo parsers; GLM's independent runtime recipe selects glm47; DeepSeek supplies encoding and protocol parsing with tool-call tests; Qwen3-Coder documents a dedicated function-call format. [uncertain] These are not proof of schema correctness or identical JSON-schema support across all candidates.
verified_findings.confidence: High for documented integration; unmeasured correctness
verified_findings.practical_implication: Test tool semantics, schemas, streaming and tool-result continuation on the selected runtime.

verified_findings.claim: BFCL V4 evaluates function calling and agentic behavior, including web search, memory and format sensitivity. Its checked leaderboard reports 2026-04-12 and a reproducibility commit/package. RULER evaluates 13 synthetic tasks across four categories with configurable length and complexity, beyond simple recall.
verified_findings.practical_implication: Use these protocols to test exact releases; do not substitute advertised maximum context for measured effective context.

verified_findings.claim: Two smaller official candidates are Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a 35B/3B-active vision-language model with thinking preservation, and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, a 30.5B/3.3B-active text coding model that supports only non-thinking mode.
verified_findings.practical_implication: Evaluate a smaller model first when local capacity or interactive response time is constrained.

deployment_requirements.documented: MiMo documents a specialized vLLM image and mimo parsers, or distributed SGLang configuration. Step documents model-supporting builds and vllm/vllm-openai:step-5-preview, with example FP8 deployments on four B300 or eight H200 GPUs. GLM recipe uses glm47 parsers and native FP8; its configuration records Transformers 5.15.0. DeepSeek's encoding/toolkit does not itself execute tools or host HTTP. These are integration evidence, not tested deployments.
deployment_requirements.version_limits: [uncertain] GLM recipe header says vLLM 0.29.0+ while prerequisites/install show 0.28.0; resolve against a pinned runtime before use. Qwen3-Coder warns Transformers below 4.51.0 lacks qwen3_moe. Windows-local serving support for these exact giant configurations was not verified.
deployment_requirements.memory_rule: All weights, auxiliary modules, cache, runtime buffers and concurrency matter. Active MoE parameters describe conditional computation; they do not mean only active weights must fit in memory.

operating_profile.status: [uncertain] No local latency, cold-start, throughput, maximum concurrent users or effective-context measurements were performed. Provider tokens/second on rankings cannot be transferred to local quantizations.
operating_profile.estimates: Derived ideal weight-only arithmetic: 30.5B parameters at two bytes/parameter is 61GB decimal; at four bits is 15.25GB. For 35B: 70GB or 17.5GB. Quantization metadata, retained higher-precision tensors, KV cache, multimodal encoders and runtime allocations add memory. These are not fit guarantees.
operating_profile.context: Start acceptance tests at 8K and 32K with one user; expand context and concurrency only after measurements. Canonical artifact revisions are recorded in candidate_comparison.

language_evidence.English: AA describes its suite as primarily English; its ranking is meaningful evidence for those evaluated tasks, with configuration caveats.
language_evidence.Finnish: [uncertain] No Finnish quality measurement for these exact pinned checkpoints was verified. Finnish is an optional evaluation example, not an assumed family requirement.
language_evidence.other_languages: GLM card declares English and Chinese; a language tag or multilingual coding benchmark does not establish conversational quality across every language. Evaluate the actual household languages.

retrieval_and_memory_design.status: Detailed extraction, embeddings, rerankers and memory access control belong to the deployment/retrieval item. Model identity alone cannot establish them.
retrieval_and_memory_design.implications: Proposed design: keep authorization and deletion in the application/storage layer, inject only the authorized user's records, and cite retrieved source spans. Long context is a capacity ceiling, not persistent memory. Test isolation with synthetic cross-user canaries; never rely on a system prompt to enforce access.

benchmark_caveats: Vendor tables are labelled vendor-measured here even when they include competitor scores. Public benchmark names do not make the vendor run independent.

Terminal-Bench 2.1, 3.0 and 4.0 are different tasks/protocols. HLE full, text-only, with tools and no-tools are distinct. A maximum reasoning-effort run can spend substantially more output tokens than another configuration.
AA v4.3.2 and BenchAlign v5.8 are different composites. BenchLM's estimated intervals do not prove rank confidence. Both can mix provider-served configurations with different runtime behavior.
[uncertain] No exact six-model BFCL or RULER comparison was verified. The checked BFCL snapshot predates several candidates. It supports methodology, not new release rankings.

Quantization, context length, prompt format, parser choice, harness retries, tool access, wall-clock budget and hidden benchmark contamination can change results. Advertised 1M context does not establish successful retrieval or reasoning at 1M.
evaluation_plan: Proposal only: freeze repository SHA, license, runtime commit/image digest, precision, parser, prompt template and decoding settings. Compare equal task/tool and wall-clock budgets, recording reasoning tokens and total tokens; use three seeds where stochastic.

Run 30 held-out coding fixes with executable tests and regression checks in a disposable sandbox. Proposed gate: at least 24 correct, zero claimed test passes without execution evidence, and no writes outside the sandbox.

Run 100 synthetic tool cases covering nested JSON schema, enums, nullable fields, parallel and sequential calls, irrelevant tools, invalid arguments, tool failure, streaming and continuation. Proposed gate: 100% parseable/schema-valid outputs and at least 95% correct action/arguments; zero unauthorized tool execution.

Use a pinned BFCL subset and report all categories separately. Use RULER at 8K/32K/64K/128K and higher only if capacity allows, plus real document multi-hop questions with evidence spans. Proposed effective-context gate: at least 90% at each required length and no more than 5 percentage-point drop from 8K; report failure length, not just maximum configured length.

Evaluate 30 household tasks per required language with bilingual review. If Finnish is required, add inflection, names, mixed English/Finnish code requests and evidence-grounded document answers; proposed gate: at least 90% adequate/correct and zero invented citations.

Test three synthetic user accounts for document/chat/tool access, cross-user canary leakage and deletion. Proposed gate: zero unauthorized disclosures; ensure deletion removes subsequent retrieval access. These system gates do not measure model weights alone.

Measure cold load, time to first token, time to complete successful tasks, p50/p95 latency, memory and failure rate at concurrency one and three. Set the acceptable latency threshold with the household before choosing a winner.

weights_and_bundled_code: MiMo: MIT is declared in card metadata; [uncertain] repository file listing has no standalone license file, so preserve that limitation and obtain official text before redistribution.
DeepSeek 1017: card explicitly applies MIT to repository and weights; actual MIT text requires preserving notice.

GLM-5.3: custom grant covers weights and inference/training code; notice retention and law compliance, plus security review for qualifying MaaS businesses above US$10B aggregate revenue over 12 months.

Kimi K3: custom grant covers weights and bundled code. Qualifying MaaS above US$20M aggregate annual revenue needs agreement; high-scale commercial UI attribution conditions also exist, with stated internal-use and certified-channel exceptions.

Qwen3.8-Max license: covers open weights/config/inference code; separate license for qualifying MaaS/AI Work Assistant businesses above US$50M aggregate annual revenue, with an internal-use exception; high-scale commercial attribution conditions also exist.

StepFun Model License 1.0: covers weights and model-specific code; notice, modification and redistribution conditions; separate license for specified commercial hardware-device embedding and qualifying MaaS above US$20M annual aggregate revenue. It explicitly includes substantial output-trained models in derivative scope.
Qwen3.6 and Qwen3-Coder: checked LICENSE files are Apache 2.0. Runtime, UI and third-party dependency licenses must be checked separately.
privacy_and_license.privacy: Local weights permit inference without sending prompts to the vendor as a design option; they do not themselves guarantee private operation. Hosted APIs, web tools and remote coding tools can transmit family data. Proposed deployment should make any egress explicit and enforce per-user authorization outside the model.
privacy_and_license.legal_limit: Conservative reading for research, not a blanket guarantee about every family/commercial configuration. [uncertain] API privacy/retention terms were not audited in this item.

recommendation.practical_default: Conditionally evaluate Qwen3.6-35B-A3B for the general assistant and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as a coding baseline. Their official artifacts and clear Apache licenses make useful initial evaluation candidates; no household hardware or response speed is assumed.
recommendation.stronger_option: If the hardware item establishes capacity, compare pinned MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 under one harness. MiMo is a defensible ranking-led candidate; GLM and DeepSeek are coding/tool candidates. The research does not identify a universal winner.
recommendation.other_candidates: Retain Step and Kimi when their task strengths justify the operating and license constraints. Treat local Qwen3.8 and hosted Max as distinct options; use API benchmark results only after verifying checkpoint equivalence.
recommendation.decision_changes: Choose the smallest model that passes household task, language, tool, privacy and latency gates. A larger model's controlled success advantage, resolved license/runtime gaps, or hardware measurements could change that choice.

next_steps: Resolve MiMo license text, API/checkpoint mapping and required modalities; obtain a vendor statement rather than infer from shortened names.
Resolve GLM counting/version inconsistencies and DeepSeek full parameter/storage accounting with the hardware researcher.
Confirm household hardware, simultaneous users, task mix, language needs and response-time targets before implementation.
Design the held-out evaluation pack and choose exact runtime/parser combinations; do not install or download during this research phase.
Compare one smaller baseline first, then escalate to giant candidates only if the measured success gap justifies capacity.
Record an evidence snapshot for every future ranking: date, evaluator version, exact model/reasoning effort, provider and artifact mapping.
open_questions: [uncertain] Does Xiaomi publish full MIT text or an official statement explicitly covering this RL artifact? Its metadata tag alone is weaker than a license file.
[uncertain] Are MiMo API, AA evaluation endpoint and RL weights functionally identical? A checkpoint mapping or reproducible endpoint-to-artifact evaluation is needed.
[uncertain] What explains GLM's 743B/39B versus 753B/40B counts, and which minimum vLLM build is correct?
[uncertain] What is DeepSeek 1017's complete parameter and stored-tensor accounting including Engram, draft heads and vision? Do not erase the discrepancy with arithmetic alone.
[uncertain] What exact protocols produce the original MiMo 49.4/Kimi 46.9 HLE claims? Need source rows and subset/tool settings.
[uncertain] Is any Kimi hosted endpoint deprecated? Need a vendor lifecycle notice; accessible weights do not answer API status.
[uncertain] Exact Finnish quality, BFCL scores, effective long context and quantized local performance remain unmeasured for these revisions.
